data_description.margin_w: Watts left unrouted so measurement noise and latency do not turn into grid import.
data_description.offpeak_budget_w: Total power the off-peak top-up may feed at once. 0 = one device at a time. Set your subscribed power minus the rest of the site to let several chargers or water heaters run together.
data_description.subscription_va: The most the house may draw. When set, everything solarprio feeds from the grid on purpose (off-peak, sanitary) is limited to what is left under this value after the rest of the house, and nothing is fed from the grid if the house power is unknown. Leave empty for no limit. Needs the house power sensor below.
data_description.house_entity: For example the power drawn from the grid on your meter. Needed for the limit above.
data_description.emergency_import_w: If more than this is drawn from the grid (not counting what is fed from the grid on purpose), every device running on the sun is switched off at once. Leave empty to turn it off.
data_description.stale_after_s: Seconds without an update after which the measurement counts as lost. 0 = never judge by age, only by availability: use it when your sensor does not report a value that does not change (the panel then shows "has not reported for N s" for a perfectly healthy sensor).
data_description.offpeak_entity: The entity that tells when the tariff is off-peak, for example your Linky tariff period (a sensor that reads HC.. or HP..), a binary sensor or a boolean. NOT an energy index (a number that only grows). Devices that follow the site off-peak hours use it.
data_description.offpeak_values: Which states mean off-peak, comma separated. Leave empty for HC.. style tariff periods, "on" or "true". Example: HC*
data_description.offpeak: Local time, 24 h, comma separated, for example 22:30-06:30 (a window may cross midnight). Devices that follow the site off-peak hours are fed in these windows. If you also give the signal entity, BOTH must say off-peak.
data_description.offpeak_extra: More windows, for example the midday off-peak hours 12:30-14:30. They count only while the "extra off-peak windows" switch of a device is on, so each device can choose.

entities.description: Energy dashboard: grid power sensor {grid}, solar power sensor {solar} ("-" = none usable; a number = that many grid sensors, pre-filled only when there is exactly one). The dashboard counts power drawn from the grid as positive, so "My meter reports import as positive" is pre-set when its grid sensor is used.

error.invalid: Invalid value: check the off-peak windows (for example 22:30-06:30), and that a subscription limit comes with the house power sensor.

data.name: Name
data.scale: Value sent to the number entity
data.soc_resume_margin: Resume charging this far below the limit (%)
data.stay_tolerance_w: Grid import tolerated to keep running
data.done_below_w: Finished when consumption falls to (W, 0 = 5 % of the power)
data.done_after_s: Check for finished only after it has run for
data.temp_max_solar: Stop heating with the sun at (°C)
data.temp_max_offpeak: Stop heating in off-peak hours at (°C)
data.temp_min: Sanitary minimum (°C), heated from the grid below it
data.offpeak_extra: Extra off-peak windows (optional, with a switch)
data.sanitary_forced_only: Sanitary minimum only on a forced run

data_description.entity_id: On/off and adjustable: the entity to switch or set. Battery: the number entity of the charge setpoint. EV charger: the number entity of the charging current in amps. Task: a helper (input_boolean) that your own scripts read; solarprio never switches a power supply for a task. Do not use an on/off load for a computer, server or NAS: cutting their power can lose data.
data_description.scale: percent: 0-100 of the maximum power. watts: power in W.
data_description.soc_max: Without a state of charge sensor, a limit below 100 means the device will not charge.
data_description.min_current_a: 6 A is the usual minimum for AC charging (IEC 61851-1); check your charger.
data_description.measured_entity: Real power drawn. Lets the engine free surplus when the device takes less than commanded.
data_description.connected_entity: on = plugged in. Unknown is treated as plugged in. An unplugged car gets nothing, so the surplus goes to lower priorities.
data_description.switch_entity: If set, the charger is switched on/off with it. Otherwise it is paused by setting 0 A (not every charger accepts that).
data_description.phases: Fixed number of phases. Automatic 1/3 phase switching is not supported.
data_description.offpeak: Local time, 24 h, comma separated, for example 22:30-06:30, 12:30-14:30 (a window may cross midnight). In these windows the device is fed at full power, whatever the sun does, until it stops consuming or the water is hot; then the next device in priority order takes its turn. If you also fill the signal entity below, BOTH must say off-peak (for example only the night hours of the tariff).
data_description.reset_at: HH:MM. A device found finished is topped up again from this time. Default: the end of the first window, so once a day.
data_description.done_below_w: Measured power at or below which the device counts as finished.
data_description.done_after_s: Seconds the device must have been on before a low consumption means finished (slow sensors, inrush).
data_description.offpeak_entity: An entity that tells when the tariff is off-peak, for example the tariff period of your Linky (a sensor whose state looks like HC.. or HP..), a binary sensor or a boolean. NOT an energy index: that one is a number that only grows. The top-up runs while it says off-peak, and each new off-peak period tries the device again. Unknown or unavailable never starts anything.
data_description.offpeak_values: Comma separated states that mean off-peak, for example HC.. or HC* (the star stands for anything after HC). Check the real state of your entity in Developer tools > States. Empty: on, true, HC, HC.., and any text containing creuse (case-insensitive).
data_description.power_w: Maximum power of the load. For a task: an estimate of what the tasks it allows will draw (used to decide when there is enough surplus).
data_description.temp_entity: The temperature of the tank or of the heated water. It is needed for the temperature limits below: without it solarprio cannot tell when the water is hot, so a device that has temperature limits gets no power while the reading is missing.
data_description.temp_max_solar: With the sun, heating stops above this temperature and starts again when the water has cooled by the hysteresis. Leave empty for no limit.
data_description.temp_max_offpeak: Same for the off-peak top-up and is usually a bit lower. Leave empty to use the value above.
data_description.temp_hysteresis: How far the water must cool below a limit before heating starts again. 3 °C is a good start.
data_description.temp_min: If the water falls under this temperature it is heated from the grid, whatever the sun or the hours, until it is back above it plus the hysteresis (the hot-water safety against bacteria is usually 40 to 60 °C: check what your installer advises). Leave empty to never heat from the grid for this reason. Needs a temperature sensor and, to be safe on a small subscription, the house power sensor of the site settings.
data_description.surplus_only: Forbids everything that feeds this device from the grid: no off-peak top-up and no sanitary heating. Only solar surplus is used.
data_description.hold_s: After the power of this device changed, wait this long before raising it again (half of it before lowering it). The grid measurement needs a few seconds to show the effect of a change; without waiting the regulation overshoots and imports from the grid. 8 seconds suits a dimmer on a Linky.
data_description.ramp_up_w: The power never rises by more than this at once, so a big surplus is followed in steps. 200 W is a good start for a dimmer. Leave empty for no limit.
data_description.deadband_w: Do not change the power for a few watts: it only wears the equipment and makes the measurement hunt. Going to or from zero is never ignored.
data_description.offpeak_extra: Same format as the windows above, for example 12:30-14:30 for the midday off-peak hours. They count as off-peak only while the "extra windows" switch of this device is on (created by solarprio), so you can choose from Home Assistant whether to heat at midday. If you also fill the signal entity, both must still say off-peak.
data_description.sanitary_forced_only: The sanitary minimum (see "Sanitary minimum" above) heats from the grid only while the "forced run" switch of this device is on. Without this option it heats automatically whenever the water is too cold.
data_description.offpeak_site: The device is fed from the grid in the off-peak hours set in the Settings of the site (signal entity, windows and extra windows). The hours are set once there, for every device: this is the only place. A device that does not tick this is not fed in off-peak hours.

import_energy.title: Import from the Energy dashboard
import_energy.description: Name and power sensor are taken from the dashboard; you then choose the entity to control and the power of each device.

copy_select.title: Copy a device
copy_select.description: Opens a new device with the same settings (power, timers, off-peak). You only choose its name and entities.

error.invalid_device: Invalid device: power must be > 0 and minimum power cannot exceed it. Off-peak: use windows like 22:30-06:30 OR a signal entity (not both), and a measured power sensor; a battery cannot have them.

options.on_off: On/off load (water heater, heater, pump, socket)
options.task: Computing task (go signal, never a power switch)

options.water_heater_dimmer: Water heater on a solar router (dimmer, adjustable power)
options.water_heater_relay: Water heater on a relay or contactor (on/off)

state.no_cap: Forced run refused: set a subscription limit
